subject: MAP milestone: loadwave slotting & ops dependencies
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Zhou <e.zhou@helioshealth.com>, Aaron Price <aaron@helioshealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MAP milestone: loadwave slotting & ops dependencies

Thanks again for the call this morning — quick recap and a couple of concrete asks so we can lock the MAP milestone for the load/perf test. High level: Helios wants a traffic replay that emulates the June 2027 peak (approx. 18k requests/min peak, sustained 4–6 minutes bursts), and latency SLO target is p95 < 220ms for the end-to-end request path.

Proposed milestone items and owners (draft):
- Test window (Helios): preferred slot 2027-09-22 02:00–06:00 UTC (US overnight). 
- Redwood responsibilities (Sergio / Marissa): provision dedicated cluster, pre-warm KV cache, run smoke, collect token-level cost breakdown.
- Helios responsibilities (Elaine / Aaron): provide a short replay manifest (traffic_profile_v3.json), grant egress rules for our test agents to call the staging endpoint, designated Ops lead for cutover and monitoring.

Sizing asks (initial):
- Target dedicated sizing: 4 x H100-80GB (estimate) for peak throughput; we can scale to 6 nodes if replay shows hotter tails. Goal is to keep p95 < 220ms and p99 < 600ms.

Open dependencies / blockers:
1) Replay dataset and exact QPS curve (we only have summary numbers). Attach traffic_profile_v3.json — pls confirm the payload mix and percent bot traffic.
2) Network egress / firewall allowlist for our testips.redwood.ai agent pool.
3) Confirmation of a Helios Ops contact who can trigger load and monitor backend health during the window.

Next steps: can you confirm the window above or propose two alternate 4-hour slots this week? Also flag who will be your on-call for the run. Once we have that, Marissa will draft a one-page runbook and I’ll update the MAP spreadsheet (attached) with the milestone and target close date.

Attachments: MAP_v2.xlsx (draft milestone table), traffic_profile_v3.json (sample replay manifest)

Thanks,
Sergio
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0124

From: Elaine Zhou <e.zhou@helioshealth.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Aaron Price <aaron@helioshealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-11T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP milestone: loadwave slotting & ops dependencies

Thanks Sergio — that all looks good and very actionable. Quick responses: 
- Window: 2027-09-22 02:00–06:00 UTC works for our team — we can make the endpoint read-only and run the replay against our staging cluster. If something blocks, alternate windows are 2027-09-23 02:00–06:00 UTC or 2027-09-24 22:00–02:00 UTC.
- Dataset/manifest: I attached our internal replay manifest excerpt (see traffic_profile_v3.json you included; we’ll add detailed payload mix and mark spike segments).
- Ops lead: Aaron will be the primary on-call during the window (aaron@helioshealth.com). He’ll also coordinate with infra to snapshot metrics and provide access to the staging Grafana.
- Security: We will open the allowlist for your test agent IP range for the duration of the window — I’ll send the request to Infra after we finalize the MAP milestone.

One ask from our side: we’d like Redwood to run a 30–45 minute warmup with the same user prefixes to populate caches and KV store before the measured run. Can you confirm how you handle cache pre-fill and warmup? Also please surface any quota or billing implications for the warmup run so we can reflect it in the MAP.

Happy to proceed on the 22nd; Aaron — will you confirm?

Best,
Elaine
Director, Product Operations | Helios Health
elaine.zhou@helioshealth.com

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elaine Zhou <e.zhou@helioshealth.com>, Aaron Price <aaron@helioshealth.com>
Date: 2027-09-11T12:30:00-07:00
Subject: FW: MAP milestone: loadwave slotting & ops dependencies

Marissa / Karthik — forwarding Elaine’s confirmation. Two internal asks for the runbook and capacity plan before I lock the MAP milestone in the spreadsheet: 
1) Capacity recommendation: Elaine asked for a warmup and we want to size dedicated nodes conservatively. Please provide a short recommendation: H100 vs A100 count for the 18k rpm peak (include expected sustained QPS and headroom for spikes). If you have a quick cost estimate for the 4-hour window (including warmup), include that too.
2) Warmup approach: Marissa please outline steps to prefill prefixes and KV cache (target duration, whether we simulate user embeddings, and any tooling we run to avoid cold-start artifacts).

I’ll include both items in the MAP_v2.xlsx and ping Helios for final signoff. Low priority but helpful: highlight anything that requires a separate procurement or SLA exception (e.g., reserving dedicated capacity outside standard hours).

Thanks — Sergio

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elaine Zhou <e.zhou@helioshealth.com>, Aaron Price <aaron@helioshealth.com>
Date: 2027-09-12T09:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FW: MAP milestone: loadwave slotting & ops dependencies

Quick ops plan and sizing note below. I attached a runnable runbook template (redwood-runbook-template.md) that we can tailor to Helios.

Sizing (initial, conservative):
- Starting point: 4 x H100-80GB across 2 inference shards. Estimated sustained QPS: ~350–420 QPS sustained across the cluster; short bursts to 600 QPS tolerated with headroom. This aligns with the 18k rpm peak (300 RPS avg during peak minutes, with burst segments).
- If Helios expects heavier request payloads or longer context lengths, bump to 6 x H100.
- If budget is a hard constraint, 6 x A100-80GB is a cost-efficient alternative with slightly higher latency at p95 (expected +30–60ms).

Warmup / KV prefill approach:
- Planned warmup window: 45 minutes prior to the measured run. Steps:
  1) Run prefix-warm script to generate representative prefix tokens and populate KV cache for top 80% of prefixes (script references attached in the runbook).
  2) Execute a 15-minute medium-intensity smoke (approx. 40% of peak QPS) to validate routing, autoscaling damper, and metrics ingestion.
  3) Trigger full-profile replay for 5 minutes (not counted in measured run) to observe tail latencies and verify model throughput.
- Tooling: we will use our replay-agent (TLS-auth) with the provided traffic_profile_v3.json. We require Helios to share the full payload samples for accurate encoding size estimates.

Cost note: estimated infra burn for the entire 5-hour engagement (warmup + measurement + buffer) on 4 x H100 is ~USD 9k–12k depending on region and spot availability. We’ll pin final numbers after Helios confirms exact payload sizes.

Operational asks for Helios ahead of the window:
- Provide the final replay manifest with payload samples 72 hours prior.
- Confirm allowlist timeframe and any egress restrictions.
- Assign a metric owner to share Grafana read-only link.

I’ll add these bullets to the MAP_v2.xlsx and set target close date to 2027-09-25 unless Helios requests acceleration.

—Marissa
Head of Performance Engineering | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

If you can send the final MAP (updated MAP_v2.xlsx) and the redwood runbook filled with contact details and step timings by Tuesday 09/14, we’ll sign-off and create the infra change ticket.

Thanks — Aaron
